# Marginalia

The first correction appeared in October, in a copy of *The Sea Around Us* that had been on the shelf since Marguerite's predecessor retired. A pencilled note in the margin of page 47: *Tides in the Bay of Fundy reach 16 meters, not 12. Check your sources.*

The handwriting was small and slanted, the pencil pressed so lightly it was almost apologetic. Marguerite found it while shelving returns on a Tuesday morning, when the Kettle Harbor branch library smelled of damp carpet from the weekend rain and the radiator was clanking its usual complaint.

She should have been annoyed. Writing in library books was a small vandalism, a breach of the social contract. Instead, she caught herself smiling. The note was *correct*—she looked it up at the reference desk between helping a teenager print out a college application and showing Mrs. Aldous how to enlarge text on her e-reader. The Bay of Fundy tides did reach sixteen meters.
